newsitem.title: USA: Magna to buy back shrs after Homeland deal.
newsitem.headline: Magna to buy back shrs after Homeland deal.

text.p: Magna Group Inc said Monday it will buy back 600,000 shares of the stock it plans to issue under the terms of its proposed $216 million purchase of Homeland Bankshares Corp.

In materials prepared for a conference call on Monday, St. Louis-based Magna said the deal would dilute 1997 earnings of the combined banks by $0.07 a share, or three percent of consensus earnings estimates, while adding $0.02 a share in 1998, or 0.8 percent of consensus, and $0.04 a share in 1999, or 1.4 percent of consensus.

The earnings assumptions factor in $2.3 million in cost savings in 1997, $5.0 million in cost savings in 1998 and $5.1 million in 1999, the materials showed. The assumptions also assume the writeoff of about $5.0 million annually in goodwill generated by the purchase accounting method.
Magna said it would issue 5.0 million shares of stock and $92.0 million in cash to Homeland shareholders under terms of the deal.
Also under terms of the deal, Homeland can opt out of the deal if Magna's stock price falls below $20 a share and if Magna's stock underperforms an index of banks by more than 15 percent.
Magna was down 1/2 at 24-3/8 on Tuesday. Homeland was up 2-1/4 at 36-1/4.
